value.body: PLAB (Professional and Linguistic Assessments Board) is the General Medical Council's test for doctors with medical degrees from outside the UK. Passing PLAB 1 (a written exam) and PLAB 2 (a clinical OSCE in the UK) is one route to GMC registration with a licence to practise. Registration lets you apply for UK jobs; it does not guarantee a training post.

items.label: Stages
items.note: PLAB 1 must be passed before booking PLAB 2

items.label: English requirement
items.value: IELTS Academic 7.5 overall (7.0 each) or OET Medicine grade B

items.label: Exam fees
items.note: Plus travel, visa and UK stay costs

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A primary medical qualification from a school listed in the World Directory of Medical Schools, a completed internship, and the GMC's English-language standard. Pass PLAB 1 (offered in India and other countries), then PLAB 2 in the UK, then apply for GMC registration with a licence to practise.

value.title: At a glance
items: The UK's Medical Training (Prioritisation) Act 2026 gives UK graduates and certain other groups priority for foundation and specialty training places.
Many international graduates start in non-training (trust-grade) posts while applying for training.
Total costs — exams, English test, travel and a UK stay for PLAB 2 — add up to a substantial sum before any job offer.
